title.en: Volume 116 Book of Later Zhou 18: Shizong Annals 3
title.raw: 卷一百十六 周書7: 世宗本紀三 Volume 116 Book of Later Zhou 18: Shizong Annals 3

sentences.zh: 顯德三年春正月乙未朔，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande, spring, first month, on the first day yimao, the emperor did not receive court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande, on the first day of the first month of spring, the emperor declined the usual New Year's court homage.

sentences.zh: 前司空蘇禹珪卒。

translations.literal: The former Minister of Works Su Yugui died.
translations.idiomatic: Former Minister of Works Su Yugui died.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，李穀奏，破淮賊於上窯。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Li Gu reported defeating the Huainan rebels at Shangyao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Li Gu reported a victory over the Huainan rebels at Shangyao.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，發丁夫十萬城京師羅城。

translations.literal: On wuxu, one hundred thousand corvée laborers were levied to fortify the outer wall of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the court mobilized a hundred thousand corvée laborers to build up the capital's outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔取此月八日幸淮南。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict set the eighth day of this month for the imperial progress to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict scheduled the eighth of the month for the emperor's departure for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 殿中監馬從赟免所居官，坐幹沒外孫女霍氏之資產，為人所訟故也。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Domestic Service Ma Congyun was removed from office for having embezzled the property of his granddaughter by marriage, the Huo family, because someone had brought suit.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Congyun, director of the palace domestic service, was dismissed from office for embezzling assets belonging to his granddaughter by marriage, the Huo family, after a lawsuit was brought against him.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以宣徽南院使向訓為權東京留守，以端明殿學士王樸為副留守。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting eastern-capital regent, and Academician of the Duanming Hall Wang Pu was made deputy regent.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Xiang Xun of the southern palace secretariat bureau was appointed acting regent of the eastern capital, with Wang Pu of the Duanming Hall as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，車駕發京師，丁未，李穀奏，自壽州引軍退守正陽。

translations.literal: On renyin, the imperial carriage departed the capital; on dingwei, Li Gu reported that he had withdrawn his army from Shou Prefecture to hold Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the emperor left the capital; on dingwei Li Gu reported that he had pulled his forces back from Shouzhou to defend Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，李重進奏，大破淮賊於正陽，斬首二萬餘級，伏屍三十里，臨陣斬賊大將劉彥貞，生擒偏將鹹師朗已下，獲戎甲三十萬副、馬五百匹。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Li Chongjin reported a great defeat of the Huainan rebels at Zhengyang: more than twenty thousand heads taken, corpses strewn for thirty li; in battle the rebel great general Liu Yanzhen was beheaded, and the deputy general Xian Shilang and others were captured alive; three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses were seized.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Li Chongjin reported a crushing victory at Zhengyang over the Huainan rebels—over twenty thousand heads, corpses littering thirty li of ground. Liu Yanzhen, the enemy's chief commander, was slain in the fighting; deputy commanders including Xian Shilang were taken alive, along with three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 先是，李穀駐軍於壽春城下，以攻其城，既而淮南援軍大至，乃與將佐謀曰：「賊軍舟棹將及正陽，我師無水戰之備，萬一橋梁不守，則大軍隔絕矣，不如全師退守正陽浮橋，以俟鑾輅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Gu had encamped his army below Shouchun city to attack it; then Huainan reinforcements arrived in great numbers, and he consulted his officers, saying: "The rebel fleet will soon reach Zhengyang; our army has no preparation for naval combat—if by any chance the bridge is not held, the main force will be cut off. It is better to withdraw the whole army to guard the floating bridge at Zhengyang and await the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Gu had besieged Shouchun, but when large Huainan reinforcements arrived he told his officers: "The enemy fleet is nearing Zhengyang and we are not equipped for river fighting. If the bridge should fail, the main army would be stranded. Better to pull back in full strength to the floating bridge at Zhengyang and wait for the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆以為然，遂燔其糧草而退。

translations.literal: " All the generals agreed, and they burned their grain and fodder and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all agreed, burned their stores, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 軍回之際無復嚴整，公私之間頗多亡失，淮北役夫亦有陷於賊境者。

translations.literal: On the march back discipline was no longer strict; between public and private property there were many losses, and corvée laborers north of the Huai also fell into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: The withdrawal was disorderly; public and private property alike suffered heavy losses, and corvée workers north of the Huai were also caught behind enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，急詔侍衛都指揮使李重進率師赴之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he urgently ordered the commander-in-chief of the palace guards Li Chongjin to lead troops to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor urgently ordered Li Chongjin, commander of the palace guards, to march to their relief.

sentences.zh: 時淮賊乘李穀退軍之勢，發戰棹數百艘沿淮而上，且張斷橋之勢，彥貞以大軍列陣而進。

translations.literal: At that time the Huainan rebels, taking advantage of Li Gu's withdrawal, launched several hundred warships up the Huai and also deployed to sever the bridge; Yanzhen advanced with his main army in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan rebels exploited Li Gu's retreat, sending hundreds of warships up the Huai while positioning to cut the bridge; Yanzhen advanced with the main army in battle order.

sentences.zh: 李重進既至正陽，聞淮軍在近，率諸將渡橋而進，與賊軍遇，重進等合勢擊之，一鼓而敗之。

translations.literal: When Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang and heard the Huai army was near, he led his generals across the bridge to advance; they met the rebel army, and Chongjin and the others combined their strength and struck—one drum-roll and the enemy was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang, learned the Huai army was close, and led his generals across the bridge to engage. They met the enemy head-on and, combining forces, routed them at the first clash.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：世宗親征，行至圉鎮，聞蒨軍卻，意唐兵必追之，遣李重進急趨正陽，曰：「唐兵且至，宜急擊之。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》: Shizong campaigned in person; when he reached the town of Yu and heard that Qian's army had withdrawn, he expected Tang troops would pursue and sent Li Chongjin in haste to Zhengyang, saying: "Tang troops are about to arrive—you should strike quickly."
translations.idiomatic: (Per Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》: Shizong marched in person. At Yu Town he heard that Li Gu's army had pulled back and expected Zhou forces would pursue, so he sent Li Chongjin hurrying to Zhengyang with the words, "The Zhou army is coming—strike at once."

sentences.zh: 」彥貞等聞蒨退軍，皆以為怯，裨將鹹師朗曰：「追之可大獲。

translations.literal: " When Yanzhen and the others heard that Qian had withdrawn, they all thought him cowardly; the deputy general Xian Shilang said: "If we pursue, we can gain a great prize."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen and his officers, hearing of Li Gu's retreat, took it for cowardice. Deputy commander Xian Shilang said, "A pursuit would bring rich spoils."

sentences.zh: 」劉仁贍使人喻之曰：「君來赴援，未交戰而敵人退，不可測也，慎勿追逐。

translations.literal: " Liu Renzhan sent someone to instruct him, saying: "You came to give aid; the enemy withdrew before any battle was joined—their intent cannot be gauged. Be careful not to pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renzhan sent word: "You came as reinforcements; the enemy withdrew without fighting—their intentions are unclear. Do not pursue."

sentences.zh: 君為大將，安危以之，脫有不利，大事去矣。

translations.literal: You are the chief commander; the army's safety or ruin rests on you. If anything goes wrong, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: As supreme commander, the army's fate rests on you. One setback could lose us everything.

sentences.zh: 」前軍張全約亦曰：「不可追。

translations.literal: " The vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue also said: "Do not pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue likewise urged, "Do not pursue."

sentences.zh: 」彥貞曰：「軍容在我，汝輩何知？

translations.literal: " Yanzhen said: "Military bearing is mine to decide—what do you people know?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen retorted, "Command is mine—what do you know?"

sentences.zh: 沮吾事者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever thwarts my plan—beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who blocks me will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」比至正陽，而重進先至，未及食而戰。

translations.literal: " By the time they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin had already arrived; before they could eat, battle was joined.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin was already there; they had not even eaten before the fighting began.

sentences.zh: 彥貞施利刃於拒馬，又刻木為獸，號捷馬牌，以皮囊布鐵蒺藜於地。

translations.literal: Yanzhen fitted chevaux-de-frise with sharp blades, also carved wooden beasts called "swift-horse boards," and spread caltrops from leather sacks upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen armed his abatis with blades, set up carved wooden beasts called "swift-horse boards," and strewed caltrops from leather bags across the field.

sentences.zh: 周兵見而知其怯，一鼓而敗之，彥貞死於陣。）〉

translations.literal: The Zhou troops saw this and knew their enemy was timid; one drum-roll and they were defeated, and Yanzhen died on the field.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou soldiers saw these devices and knew their foe lacked nerve; one charge routed them, and Yanzhen fell in battle.)〉

sentences.zh: 殺獲之外，降者三千餘人，皆為我將趙晁所殺。

translations.literal: Apart from those killed and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were all put to death by our general Zhao Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the dead and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were all slaughtered by our general Zhao Chao.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，車駕至正陽。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the imperial carriage reached Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the emperor arrived at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛都指揮使李重進為淮南道行營都招討使，命宰臣李穀判壽州行府事。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief of the palace guards Li Chongjin was made overall commander of the Huainan circuit campaign headquarters; the chief minister Li Gu was ordered to administer the Shou Prefecture field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, commander of the palace guards, was appointed overall commander of the Huainan campaign, and chief minister Li Gu was assigned to run the field headquarters at Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，車駕渡淮。

translations.literal: On yimao, the imperial carriage crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor crossed the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至壽州城下，營於州西北淝水之陽，詔移正陽浮橋於下蔡。

translations.literal: On bingchen, he reached below Shou Prefecture city and encamped on the south bank of the Fei River northwest of the prefecture; an edict ordered the floating bridge at Zhengyang moved to Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he camped south of the Fei River northwest of Shouzhou and ordered the Zhengyang pontoon bridge relocated to Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 庚申，耀兵於城下。

translations.literal: On gengshen, troops were displayed in force below the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he paraded his army before the city walls.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《春明退朝錄》云：家有《範魯公雜錄》，記世宗親征忠正，駐蹕城下，中夜有白虹自淝水起，亙數丈，下貫城中，數刻方沒。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Record of Leaving Court at Chunming》 says: Our family possesses the 《Miscellaneous Records of Duke Fan of Lu》, which records that when Shizong campaigned in person against Zhongzheng and halted below the city, at midnight a white rainbow rose from the Fei River, spanning several zhang, and pierced down into the city; after several moments it vanished.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of Leaving Court at Chunming》 notes that a family copy of the 《Miscellaneous Records of Duke Fan of Lu》 records how, during Shizong's personal campaign against Zhongzheng, a white rainbow rose from the Fei at midnight, arched several zhang across the sky, and plunged into the city before fading moments later.)〉

sentences.zh: 壬戌，今上奏，破淮賊萬餘眾於渦口，斬偽兵馬都監何延錫等，獲戰船五十艘。

translations.literal: On renxu, the present sovereign reported defeating more than ten thousand Huainan rebels at Wokou, beheading the false army-and-horse overseer He Yanshi and others, and capturing fifty warships.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Zhao Kuangyin reported routing over ten thousand Huainan rebels at Wokou, killing the enemy overseer of horses He Yanshi and others, and seizing fifty warships.

sentences.zh: 二月丙寅，幸下蔡。

translations.literal: Second month, bingyin: the emperor visited Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingyin, the emperor went to Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 斬前濟州馬軍都指揮使康儼於路左，坐橋道不謹也。

translations.literal: The former commander of the Jizhou horse army Kang Yan was beheaded at the roadside for negligence regarding bridges and roads.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yan, former commander of the Jizhou horse army, was beheaded by the roadside for failing to secure the bridges and roads.

sentences.zh: 朗州節度使王進逵奏，領兵入淮南界。

translations.literal: The military governor of Lang Prefecture Wang Jinkui reported leading troops into Huainan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinkui, military governor of Langzhou, reported leading his troops into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廬壽巡檢使司超奏，破淮賊三千於盛唐，獲都監偽吉州刺史高弼以獻。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Lushou inspection commissioner Si Chao reported defeating three thousand Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang and capturing the overseer, the false Jizhou prefect Gao Bi, whom he presented.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, inspection commissioner Si Chao reported defeating three thousand Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang and presenting the captured enemy overseer and false prefect of Jizhou, Gao Bi.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張昭奏，準詔撰集兵法，分為十卷，凡四十二門，目之為《制旨兵法》，上之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Zhao memorialized that, by imperial order, he had compiled military methods in ten juan, forty-two sections in all, entitled the 《Imperially Directed Art of War》, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Zhao presented the 《Imperially Directed Art of War》, a ten-juan compilation of forty-two chapters on military method that he had assembled by imperial command.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒美，仍以器幣賜之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised him, and he was also granted vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a commendatory edict and bestowed ritual vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 壬申，今上奏，破淮賊萬五千人於清流山，乘勝攻下滁州，擒偽命江州節度使、充行營應援使皇甫暉，常州團練使、充應援都監姚鳳以獻。

translations.literal: On renshen, the present sovereign reported defeating fifteen thousand Huainan rebels at Qingliushan, then pressing the victory to take Chuzhou and capture the falsely appointed Jiangzhou military governor and campaign relief commissioner Huangfu Hui, and the Changzhou defense commissioner and relief overseer Yao Feng, whom he presented.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Zhao Kuangyin reported routing fifteen thousand Huainan rebels at Qingliushan, then storming Chuzhou and capturing Huangfu Hui, the enemy's Jiangzhou governor and relief commissioner, and Yao Feng, defense commissioner of Changzhou and relief overseer, whom he sent to court.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （王钅至《默記》：李景聞世宗親至淮上，而滁州其控扼，且援壽州，命大將皇甫暉、監軍姚鳳提兵十萬扼其地。

translations.literal: (Wang Zhi's 《Silent Records》: Li Jing heard that Shizong had come in person to the Huai; Chuzhou was the strategic choke point and also relieved Shou Prefecture, so he ordered the great generals Huangfu Hui and the army overseer Yao Feng to lead one hundred thousand troops to hold the place.)
translations.idiomatic: (Per Wang Zhi's 《Silent Records》: When Li Jing learned that Shizong had reached the Huai in person, he sent Huangfu Hui and army overseer Yao Feng with a hundred thousand men to hold Chuzhou, the key to the region and a lifeline for Shouzhou.)

sentences.zh: 太祖以周師數千與暉遇於清流關隘路，周師大敗，暉整全師入憩滁州城下，會翊日再出。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor with several thousand Zhou troops met Hui at the Qingliu Pass defile; the Zhou army suffered a great defeat. Hui re-formed his full army and entered camp to rest below Chuzhou city, intending to come out again the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu met Hui at Qingliu Pass with only a few thousand Zhou troops and was badly beaten. Hui brought his intact army to camp below Chuzhou, planning to march out again the next day.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵聚關下，且虞暉兵再至，聞諸村人，雲有鎮州趙學究在村中教學，多智計，村民有爭訟者，多請以決曲直。

translations.literal: Taizu's troops gathered below the pass, fearing Hui's army would return; he asked the villagers, who said there was a Zhenzhou scholar Zhao in the village teaching school, very resourceful—when villagers had disputes they often asked him to decide right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu held the pass, anxious that Hui would return. Villagers told him of Zhao the scholar from Zhenzhou, a village schoolmaster famed for his wits, to whom locals brought disputes for judgment.

sentences.zh: 太祖往訪之，學究曰：「我有奇計，所謂因敗為勝，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Taizu went to consult him; the scholar said: "I have a strange plan—what is called turning defeat into victory and misfortune into blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sought him out. The scholar said, "I have a plan to turn defeat into victory and disaster into gain."

sentences.zh: 今關下有徑路，人無行者，雖牌軍亦不知之，乃山之背也，可以直抵城下。

translations.literal: Now below the pass there is a footpath no one uses—even the guard corps do not know it; it is on the mountain's far side and can reach the city directly.
translations.idiomatic: Below the pass is an unused trail—even the garrison guards do not know it. It runs behind the mountain straight to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 方值西澗水大漲之時，彼必謂我既敗之後，無敢躡其後者，誠能由山背小路率兵浮西澗水至城下，斬關而入，可以得志。

translations.literal: Just when the West Stream is in flood, they will surely think that after our defeat no one would dare follow them. If you can truly lead troops by the mountain's back path, ford the West Stream, reach the city, cut down the gate guards and enter, you can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The West Stream is swollen now; they will assume that after beating us no one would dare follow. Lead men along the back trail, ford the stream, break in at the gate, and you can win.

sentences.zh: 」太祖大喜，且命學究以指其路，學究亦不辭，而遣人前導，即下令誓師，夜從小徑行，三軍跨馬浮西澗以迫城，暉果不為備。

translations.literal: " Taizu was greatly pleased and ordered the scholar to point out the way; the scholar did not refuse, sent men ahead as guides, and immediately ordered the army sworn for battle; by night they took the small path, the whole army mounted and forded the West Stream to press the city—and Hui indeed was unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Taizu had the scholar guide the way. The scholar obliged, sent scouts ahead, and Taizu swore in the troops for a night march along the hidden path. The whole army forded the West Stream and closed on the city; Hui was caught completely off guard.

sentences.zh: 奪門以入，暉始聞之，率親兵擐甲與太祖巷戰，三縱而三擒之，遂下滁州。）〉

translations.literal: They seized the gate and entered; only then did Hui hear of it. He led his personal guard in armor to fight Taizu in the lanes; three times he was released and three times captured, and Chuzhou was taken.)〉
translations.idiomatic: They burst through the gate. Hui rallied his household guard for street fighting with Taizu, was captured three times after being released three times, and Chuzhou fell.)〉

sentences.zh: 甲戌，江南國主李景遣泗州牙將王知朗賫書一函至滁州，本州以聞，書稱唐皇帝奉書於大周皇帝，其略云：「願陳兄事，永奉鄰歡，設或俯鑒遠圖，下交小國，悉班卒乘，俾乂蒼黔，慶雞犬之相聞，奉瓊瑤以為好，必當歲陳山澤之利，少助軍旅之須。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Li Jing, ruler of Jiangnan, sent the Sizhou junior general Wang Zhilang bearing one letter to Chuzhou; the prefecture reported it. The letter read: "The Tang emperor presents this letter to the Great Zhou emperor," and in summary said: "I wish to declare brotherly relations and forever maintain neighborly harmony; if Your Majesty would deign to regard my distant design and condescend to treat my small state, I would deploy all soldiers and chariots to bring peace to the black-haired people, rejoice that cock and dog may hear one another across the border, offer jade and fine silks in friendship, and every year present the produce of mountains and marshes to aid somewhat the army's needs."
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Li Jing of Jiangnan sent Wang Zhilang of Sizhou with a letter to Chuzhou, which was forwarded to court. Addressed from "the Tang emperor" to "the Great Zhou emperor," it offered brotherly ties and lasting peace, pledged troops to pacify the people, jade gifts in friendship, and yearly tribute from mountain and marsh to help supply the army.

sentences.zh: 虔俟報章，以答高命，道塗朝坦，禮幣夕行」云。

translations.literal: I reverently await your reply to answer your lofty command; may the road be level by morning and gifts sent by evening," it said.
translations.idiomatic: It closed by saying he awaited a reply and that tribute would follow at once once the road was clear.

sentences.zh: 書奏不答。

translations.literal: The memorial of the letter received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court made no reply to the letter.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，今上縶送所獲江南二將皇甫暉、姚鳳至行在，詔釋之。

translations.literal: On yihai, the present sovereign sent under guard to the imperial camp the two Jiangnan generals he had captured, Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng; an edict ordered their release.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Zhao Kuangyin sent the captured Jiangnan generals Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng to the imperial camp, where an edict ordered them released.

sentences.zh: 壬午，江南國主李景遣其臣偽翰林學士戶部侍郎鐘謨、偽工部侍郎文理院學士李德明等奉表來上，敘願依大國稱臣納貢之意，仍進金器千兩，錦綺綾羅二千匹及禦衣、犀帶、茶茗、藥物等，又進犒軍牛五百頭，酒二千石。

translations.literal: On renwu, Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his ministers, the false Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhong Mo, the false Vice Minister of Works and academician of the Wenli Academy Li Deming, and others to present a memorial stating his wish to submit to the great state as vassal and offer tribute; he also sent one thousand liang of gold vessels, two thousand bolts of brocade and gauze, imperial robes, rhinoceros-horn belts, tea, medicines, and the like, and further five hundred oxen and two thousand shi of wine to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Li Jing sent Zhong Mo, Li Deming, and other ministers with a memorial offering vassal submission and tribute: a thousand liang of gold vessels, two thousand bolts of silks, imperial robes, rhinoceros belts, tea, medicines, five hundred oxen, and two thousand shi of wine for the troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，賜謨等錦綺綾羅二百匹，銀器一百兩，襲衣、金帶、鞍馬等。

translations.literal: That day, Mo and the others were granted two hundred bolts of brocade and gauze, one hundred liang of silver vessels, court robes, gold belts, saddled horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the court rewarded Mo and his party with two hundred bolts of silk, a hundred liang of silverware, robes, gold belts, and horses.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，侍衛馬軍指揮韓令坤奏，收下揚州。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the commander of the palace horse army Han Lingkun reported taking Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Han Lingkun, commander of the palace horse army, reported the capture of Yangzhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·韓令坤傳》：率兵襲揚州，將吏開門以迎之，令坤整眾而入，市不易肆，人甚悅。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》, biography of Han Lingkun: He led troops in a surprise against Yangzhou; the officers opened the gates to welcome him. Lingkun entered with his forces in good order; the markets did not change their stalls, and the people were greatly pleased.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 biography of Han Lingkun records that he stormed Yangzhou, the garrison opened the gates to him, and he entered in good order without disturbing the markets—a welcome relief to the populace.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁亥，壽州城內左神衛軍使徐象等一十八人來奔。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Xu Xiang, commissioner of the Left Divine Guard Army in Shou Prefecture city, and seventeen others came over to our side.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Xu Xiang of the Left Divine Guard and seventeen others defected from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朗州節度使王進逵上言領兵入鄂州界，攻長山寨，殺賊軍三千餘眾。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the military governor of Lang Prefecture Wang Jinkui reported leading troops into E Prefecture territory, attacking Changshan Stockade, and killing more than three thousand rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Wang Jinkui reported leading troops into Ezhou, storming Changshan Stockade, and killing over three thousand enemy soldiers.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，今上表偽命天長軍制置使耿謙以本軍降，獲糧草二千餘萬。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the present sovereign memorialized that the falsely appointed Tianchang army commissioner Geng Qian had surrendered with his command, and more than twenty million units of grain and fodder were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Zhao Kuangyin reported that Geng Qian, the enemy commissioner at Tianchang, had surrendered with his army, yielding more than twenty million units of grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤上言，泰州降。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief of the palace horse army Han Lingkun reported that Taizhou had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun, commander of the palace horse army, reported the surrender of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，荊南上言，朗州節度使王進逵為部將潘叔嗣所殺。

translations.literal: On guisi, Jingnan reported that the military governor of Lang Prefecture Wang Jinkui had been killed by his subordinate general Pan Shusi.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Jingnan reported that Wang Jinkui of Langzhou had been killed by his subordinate Pan Shusi.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王逵傳》：領眾逼宜春，道出長沙，耀兵金波亭，有蜜蜂集傘蓋中，占者以為不利，遂留長沙，令行營副使毛立領兵南下，以潘叔嗣、張文表為前鋒。

translations.literal: (The 《Record of the Nine States》, biography of Wang Kui: Leading his host to press Yichun, he passed through Changsha and displayed troops at Jinbo Pavilion; bees gathered on his parasol, and diviners deemed it ill-omened, so he remained at Changsha and ordered the deputy campaign commander Mao Li to lead troops south, with Pan Shusi and Zhang Wenbiao as vanguard.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of the Nine States》 biography of Wang Kui records that marching on Yichun via Changsha, he paraded at Jinbo Pavilion; bees swarmed his parasol, diviners called it a bad sign, so he stayed in Changsha and sent deputy Mao Li south with Pan Shusi and Zhang Wenbiao in the vanguard.)

sentences.zh: 叔嗣怒，至澧陵擁眾而還。

translations.literal: Shusi was angry; reaching Liling he gathered his troops and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shusi turned back at Liling with his troops.

sentences.zh: 逵聞兵叛，乃乘輕舸奔歸武陵，叔嗣追殺之於朗州城外。）〉

translations.literal: Kui heard the army had mutinied, boarded a light boat and fled to Wuling; Shusi pursued and killed him outside Lang Prefecture city.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Kui fled by light boat to Wuling when he heard of the mutiny; Shusi overtook and killed him outside Langzhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 遣人詣潭州，請周行逢為帥，行逢至朗州，斬叔嗣於市。

translations.literal: He sent someone to Tan Prefecture to invite Zhou Xingfeng as commander; Xingfeng reached Lang Prefecture and beheaded Shusi in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to Tanzhou inviting Zhou Xingfeng to take command; when he reached Langzhou he executed Shusi in the market.

sentences.zh: 三月丙申，行光州刺史何超奏，光州偽命都監張承翰以城歸順，尋授承翰集州刺史。

translations.literal: Third month, bingshen: the acting prefect of Guang Prefecture He Chao reported that the falsely appointed Guangzhou overseer Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon appointed prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, acting Guangzhou prefect He Chao reported that enemy overseer Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon made prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，文武百僚再上表請聽樂，詔允之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the civil and military officials again memorialized requesting permission to hear music; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, civil and military officials again petitioned to resume court music; the emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 行舒州刺史郭令圖奏，收下舒州。

translations.literal: The acting prefect of Shu Prefecture Guo Lingtu reported taking Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Shuzhou prefect Guo Lingtu reported the capture of Shuzhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《隆平集·王審琦傳》：世宗征淮，舒州堅壁不下，以郭令圖為刺史，命審琦、司超將兵攻城，一夕拔之。

translations.literal: (The 《Longping Collection》, biography of Wang Shenqi: When Shizong campaigned against the Huai, Shu Prefecture held firm and would not fall; Guo Lingtu was made prefect, and Shenqi and Si Chao were ordered to lead troops to assault the city—it was taken in one night.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Longping Collection》 biography of Wang Shenqi records that during the Huai campaign Shuzhou held out until Guo Lingtu was made prefect and Shenqi and Si Chao stormed it in a single night.)

sentences.zh: 令圖入，復見逐於郡人。

translations.literal: Lingtu entered, but was again driven out by the people of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lingtu entered the city only to be driven out again by local residents.

sentences.zh: 審琦方進軍援黃州，聞令圖被逐，乃選騎銜枚襲城，夜敗其眾而復納之。）〉

translations.literal: Shenqi was advancing to relieve Huang Prefecture; hearing that Lingtu had been expelled, he chose cavalry who took sticks in their mouths for a night assault on the city, defeated the hostile crowd, and reinstalled him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was marching to relieve Huangzhou when he learned of Lingtu's expulsion; he sent cavalry on a silent night raid, routed the rioters, and restored Lingtu to office.)〉

sentences.zh: 江南國主李景表送先隔過朝廷兵士一百五十人至行在。

translations.literal: Li Jing, ruler of Jiangnan, memorialized sending one hundred fifty soldiers of the court who had previously been cut off and detained, to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Jiangnan returned one hundred fifty Zhou soldiers who had been stranded on his side of the lines.

sentences.zh: 其軍即蜀軍也，秦、鳳之役，為王師所擒，配隸諸軍，及渡淮，輒復南逸。

translations.literal: That army was the Shu army; in the Qin-Feng campaign they had been captured by the imperial troops, assigned to various commands, and when they crossed the Huai they repeatedly fled south again.
translations.idiomatic: They were Shu troops captured in the Qin-Feng campaign, distributed among Zhou units, who had repeatedly deserted southward once they reached the Huai.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其奔竄，盡戮之。

translations.literal: The emperor, angry at their flight, had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged by their desertions, the emperor had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 丙午，江南國主李景遣其臣偽司空孫晟、偽禮部尚書王崇質等奉表來上，仍進金一千兩、銀十萬兩、羅綺二千匹，又進賞給將士茶絹金銀羅帛等。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his ministers, the false Minister of Works Sun Sheng, the false Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi, and others to present a memorial, and also sent one thousand liang of gold, one hundred thousand liang of silver, two thousand bolts of gauze and silk, and further tea, silks, gold, silver, and brocades to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Li Jing sent Sun Sheng, Wang Chongzhi, and other ministers with another memorial, along with a thousand liang of gold, a hundred thousand liang of silver, two thousand bolts of silk, and gifts of tea, silks, and precious metals for the troops.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，兩浙奏，遣大將率兵攻常州。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Two Zhes reported dispatching a great general to lead troops against Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Two Zhes reported sending a senior general with troops to attack Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 延州留後李彥頵奏，蕃眾與部民為亂，尋與兵司都監閻綰掩殺，獲其酋帥高鬧兒等十人，磔於市。

translations.literal: The Yanzhou military governor Li Yanbin reported that barbarian tribesmen and local people had risen in revolt; soon, with the army bureau overseer Yan Wan, he made a surprise attack and killed them, capturing their chieftains Gao Naor and nine others, who were dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou governor Li Yanbin reported a revolt by tribesmen and locals; with overseer Yan Wan he ambushed the rebels, captured ten chiefs including Gao Naor, and had them dismembered in public.

sentences.zh: 彥頵本賈人也，貪而好利，蕃漢之民怨其侵刻，故至於是。

translations.literal: Yanbin had originally been a merchant, greedy and fond of profit; barbarian and Chinese alike resented his exactions, and so matters came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin had been a merchant before his appointment; his greed and extortion had alienated both tribal and Chinese subjects, which led to the uprising.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，賜江南李景書曰：

translations.literal: On xinhai, an imperial letter was sent to Li Jing of Jiangnan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor sent Li Jing of Jiangnan a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 頃自有唐失禦，天步方艱，巢、蔡喪亂之餘，朱、李戰爭之後，中夏多故，六紀於茲，海縣瓜分，英豪鼎峙，自為聲教，各擅烝黎，連衡而交結四夷，乘釁而憑陵上國。

translations.literal: Recently, since Tang lost the Mandate and the imperial steps grew perilous, after the ruin of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, after the wars of Zhu and Li, the central realm has known many troubles for six decades now; the counties within the seas were carved up, heroes stood like tripods, each setting up his own culture and each monopolizing the people, forming horizontal alliances and befriending the four barbarians, seizing openings to encroach upon the central state.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang lost the Mandate and the throne fell into peril—after the catastrophes of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, after the wars of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong—the central realm has been in turmoil for sixty years. The empire was carved among rival lords, each proclaiming his own rule and people, allying with one another and with foreign powers, and pressing upon the heartland whenever chance allowed.

sentences.zh: 華風不競，否運所鐘，凡百有心，孰不興憤？

translations.literal: Chinese civilization could not contend; adverse fortune had struck its hour—among all who had hearts, who did not rise in indignation?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese order could not hold its own; ill fortune had taken hold. Who among the loyal did not burn with anger?

sentences.zh: 朕猥承先訓，恭荷永圖，德不迨於前王，道不方於往古。

translations.literal: I humbly received my predecessor's instruction and reverently bore the eternal design; my virtue does not reach the former kings, my Way is not equal to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I have humbly inherited my predecessor's charge and the dynasty's enduring design, yet my virtue falls short of the sage kings of old and my governance cannot match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 然而擅一百州之富庶，握三十萬之甲兵，且農戰交修，士卒樂用，思欲報累朝之宿怨，刷萬姓之包羞。

translations.literal: Yet I monopolize the wealth of a hundred prefectures and hold three hundred thousand armored troops; agriculture and warfare are both cultivated, soldiers are glad to serve—I mean to repay the accumulated wrongs of many reigns and wash away the shame wrapped around the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I command the wealth of a hundred prefectures and three hundred thousand armed men; agriculture and war are both in order and the troops are eager to fight. I mean to avenge the wrongs of generations and restore the people's honor.

sentences.zh: 是以踐位已來，懷安不暇，破幽、并之巨寇，收秦、鳳之全封，兵不告疲，民有餘力。

translations.literal: Therefore since I took the throne I have had no leisure for ease: I broke the great bandits of You and Bing, recovered the full territory of Qin and Feng—the army does not report exhaustion, the people still have surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have had no time for repose: I crushed the great enemies in You and Bing and recovered Qin and Feng intact. The army has not wearied and the people still have strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 一昨回軍隴上，問罪江幹，我實有辭，咎將誰執？

translations.literal: Just recently I turned the army from Longyou and called you to account on the river's bank—I truly have grounds; upon whom shall blame fall?
translations.idiomatic: Only lately I brought the army down from Longyou to call you to account on the Yangtze. My cause is just—who else is to blame?

sentences.zh: 朕親提金鼓，尋渡淮、淝，上順天心，下符人欲，前鋒所向，彼眾無遺，棄甲僵屍，動盈川谷。

translations.literal: I personally took up drum and gong and soon crossed the Huai and Fei—above, conforming to Heaven's heart; below, matching men's desires. Wherever the vanguard turned, none of their host remained; cast-off armor and stiff corpses filled valleys and streams.
translations.idiomatic: I took the field in person and crossed the Huai and Fei, with Heaven above and the people's will below. Wherever my van struck, the enemy left none alive; abandoned armor and corpses choked the valleys.

sentences.zh: 收城徇地，已過滁陽，豈有落其爪牙，折其羽翼，潰其心腹，扼其吭喉而不亡者哉！

translations.literal: Cities taken and lands overrun—we have already passed Chuyang. Can there be one whose claws are stripped, whose wings are broken, whose heart is routed, whose throat is gripped, and yet does not perish?
translations.idiomatic: We have taken cities and overrun lands as far as Chuyang. When claws are torn out, wings broken, the heart routed, and the throat seized—how can such a foe survive?

sentences.zh: 蚤者，泗州主將遞送到書一函；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Sizhou commander forwarded one letter;
translations.idiomatic: First your Sizhou commander forwarded a letter;

sentences.zh: 尋又使人鐘謨、李德明至，賫所上表及貢奉衣服腰帶、金銀器幣、茶藥牛酒等；

translations.literal: soon after, envoys Zhong Mo and Li Deming arrived, bearing the memorial you presented and tribute of robes, belts, gold and silver vessels, tea, medicines, oxen, wine, and the like;
translations.idiomatic: then Zhong Mo and Li Deming came with your memorial and gifts of robes, belts, gold and silver, tea, medicines, oxen, and wine;

sentences.zh: 今又使人孫晟等並到行朝。

translations.literal: now again envoys Sun Sheng and others have all reached the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: and now Sun Sheng and others have arrived at my camp as well.

sentences.zh: 觀其降身聽命，引咎告窮，所謂君子見機，不俟終日，茍非達識，孰能若斯？

translations.literal: Seeing you lower yourself and heed commands, confess fault and declare your extremity—this is what is called the gentleman perceiving the moment and not waiting even a full day; if not a man of penetrating insight, who could act thus?
translations.idiomatic: You humble yourself, accept blame, and plead your plight—the wise man, seeing how matters stand, does not wait until nightfall. Only a man of true discernment could act as you have.

sentences.zh: 但以奮武興戎，所以討不服；

translations.literal: Yet to rouse martial ardor and raise arms is how one punishes the unsubmissive;
translations.idiomatic: Yet arms are raised to chastise the defiant;

sentences.zh: 惇信明義，所以懷遠人。

translations.literal: to honor faith and clarify righteousness is how one win over those far away.
translations.idiomatic: while sincerity and justice are how distant peoples are won over.

sentences.zh: 五帝三王盛德大業，恒用此道，以正萬邦。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors and Three Kings, in their great virtue and great enterprise, constantly used this Way to set the myriad states aright.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors and Three Kings governed all under Heaven by this same principle of martial force tempered with righteousness.

sentences.zh: 朕今躬統戎師，龔行討伐，告於郊廟社稷，詢於將相公卿，天誘其衷，國無異論。

translations.literal: I now personally command the army and march in punitive expedition, announcing it to the suburban altars, ancestral temple, and altars of soil and grain, consulting generals, ministers, and chief officials—Heaven guides my heart, and the state has no dissenting voice.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the army in person on a punitive campaign, having announced it at the altars and consulted my generals and ministers. Heaven inclines my heart, and the court speaks with one voice.

sentences.zh: 茍不能恢復內地，申畫邊疆，便議班旋，真同戲劇，則何以光祖宗之烈，厭士庶之心，匪獨違天，兼且咈眾。

translations.literal: If I cannot recover the inner lands and redraw the frontier, yet discuss withdrawing the army—it would truly be like a play—how then could I glorify the ancestors' brilliance or satisfy officers and commoners? This would not only defy Heaven but also go against the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot recover our lost territory and secure the border, yet talk of withdrawing the army, it would be mere theater. How could I honor our ancestors or satisfy soldiers and people? That would defy Heaven and the will of the realm alike.

sentences.zh: 但以淮南部內，已定六州，盧、壽、濠、黃，大軍悉集，指期克日，拉朽焚枯，其餘數城，非足介意。

translations.literal: Yet within southern Huainan, six prefectures are already settled—Lu, Shou, Hao, Huang—the great army is all assembled, a set day appointed for capture; rotten wood will be pulled down and dry stubble burned—the remaining few cities are not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Within southern Huainan six prefectures are already secured—Lu, Shou, Hao, and Huang—and the main army is gathered for the final assault. The rest will fall like rotten timber; the few cities left are hardly worth mention.

sentences.zh: 必若盡淮甸之土地，為大國之提封，猶是遠圖，豈同迷復。

translations.literal: If you must have all the land of the Huai region as the great state's frontier, that is still a distant design—how can it be the same as deluded return?
translations.idiomatic: To demand all Huainan as Zhou territory is still a distant ambition—not the confused retreat you imagine.

sentences.zh: 如此則江南吏卒悉遣放還，江北軍民並當留住，免違物類之性，俾安鄉土之情。

translations.literal: Thus the officials and soldiers of Jiangnan would all be sent back, while the military and civilians north of the river would all remain—avoiding violation of creatures' natures and allowing attachment to native soil.
translations.idiomatic: Southern officials and troops would return south; northern soldiers and civilians would stay north—respecting natural loyalties and letting each people remain on native soil.

sentences.zh: 至於削去尊稱，願輸臣禮，非無故事，實有前規。

translations.literal: As for stripping your exalted title and wishing to offer ministerial rites—this is not without precedent; there truly are former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: As for renouncing your royal title and accepting vassal status, precedent exists for that as well.

sentences.zh: 蕭詧奉周，不失附庸之道；

translations.literal: Xiao Cha served Zhou without losing the way of a dependent state;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha served Zhou and kept the role of a loyal vassal;

sentences.zh: 孫權事魏，自同藩國之儀。

translations.literal: Sun Quan served Wei in the same rites as a feudatory state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan served Wei with the ceremonies proper to a feudatory prince.

sentences.zh: 古也雖然，今則不取，但存常號，何爽歲寒。

translations.literal: Ancient times were thus, but today I do not accept it; only keep your ordinary title—what offense against the winter cold?
translations.idiomatic: Such was antiquity, but I will not have it now. Keep your usual title—there is no shame in that.

sentences.zh: 儻堅事大之心，終不迫人於險，事資真愨，辭匪枝遊，俟諸郡之悉來，即大軍之立罷。

translations.literal: If you steadfastly maintain the heart of serving the great power, I will never drive men into peril; matters rely on true sincerity, words must not be branching evasions—when all prefectures have submitted, the great army will at once stand down.
translations.idiomatic: If you remain loyal to the great power, I will not press you to the brink. Deal in sincerity, not evasive words. When every prefecture has submitted, the army will withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 質於天地，信若丹青，我無彼欺，爾無我詐，言盡於此，更不煩雲，茍曰未然，請自茲絕。

translations.literal: Pledged before Heaven and Earth, faith like red and black ink—I will not deceive you, you will not cheat me; words end here, no further trouble of clouds. If you say it is not so, let us break off from this moment.
translations.idiomatic: I swear this before Heaven and Earth, as binding as ink on silk: no deceit on either side. I have said all I mean to say. If you disagree, let all relations end here.

sentences.zh: 竊以陽春在候，庶務縈思，願無廢於節宣，更自期於愛重。

translations.literal: I venture to think spring is at hand and many affairs entangle the mind; I wish you not to neglect moderation in regimen, and again to look to cherishing yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Spring is near and affairs press upon you; take care of your health and cherish yourself well.

sentences.zh: 音塵非遠，風壤猶殊，翹想所深，勞於夢寐。

translations.literal: Our messages are not far apart, yet winds and soil still differ; my eager longing runs deep and wearies me in dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Though we are not far apart, our lands still differ. You are much in my thoughts, even in dreams.

sentences.zh: 又賜其將佐書曰：

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to their generals and aides, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a letter to Li Jing's generals and officials, which read:

sentences.zh: 朕自類祃出師，麾旄問罪，絕長淮而電擊，指建業以鷹揚，旦夕之間，克捷相繼。

translations.literal: Since I offered at the war shrine and took the field, banners and staffs have called to account; crossing the long Huai like lightning, pointing at Jianye like a soaring hawk—in the space of morning and evening, victories follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the field from the war shrine, my banners have marched to judgment. We crossed the Huai like lightning and turned toward Jianye like a striking hawk; victories have followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 至若兵興之所自，釁起之所來，勝負之端倪，戎甲之次第，不勞盡諭，必想具知。

translations.literal: As for where arms arose, whence provocation came, the signs of victory and defeat, the sequence of armor—no need to explain fully; you surely know it all.
translations.idiomatic: How the war began, who provoked it, how battles have gone, and how our armies have advanced—you know all this without my recounting it.

sentences.zh: 近者金陵使人，繼來行闕，追悔前事，委質大朝，非無謝咎之辭，亦有罷軍之請，但以南邦之土地，本中夏之封疆，茍失克復之期，大辜朝野之望，已興是役，固不徒還，必若自淮以南，畫江為界，盡歸中國，猶是遠圖。

translations.literal: Recently envoys from Jinling have come in succession to the imperial camp, regretting past affairs and submitting to the great court—not without words of apology, and also requesting withdrawal of the army; yet the southern state's lands were originally the central realm's territory. If the deadline for recovery is missed, it greatly betrays court and people's hopes. This campaign having been raised, I will not return empty-handed. If you must draw the river as boundary from south of the Huai and return all to the central state, that is still a distant design.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Jinling have come repeatedly to express regret and sue for peace, even asking that the army withdraw. But the south was always central Chinese territory. To fail to recover it would betray the hopes of court and people alike. Having begun this campaign, I will not return empty-handed. To keep everything south of the Huai is still asking too much.

sentences.zh: 所雲願為外臣，乞比湖、浙，彼既服義，朕豈忍人，必當別議封崇，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: What you say—that you wish to be an outer minister and beg comparison with Hu and Zhe—since you have submitted to righteousness, how could I bear to press men? I shall certainly deliberate separately on enfeoffment and treat you with exceptional rites.
translations.idiomatic: You ask to become an outer vassal like the rulers of Hu and Zhe. Since you have submitted, I will not press you harshly. Your rank and honors will be settled separately and you will receive exceptional treatment.

sentences.zh: 凡爾將佐，各盡乃心，善為國家之謀，勉擇恒久之利。

translations.literal: All you generals and aides, each give your full heart, plan well for the state, and strive to choose lasting advantage.
translations.idiomatic: To all you commanders: give your full loyalty, counsel your state wisely, and choose what will bring lasting good.

sentences.zh: 初，李景遣鐘謨、李德明奉表至行闕，使人面奏云：「本國主願割壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海六州之地，歸於大朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Jing sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial to the imperial camp; the envoy reported in person: "Our ruler wishes to cede the six prefectures Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to the great court."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jing had sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial offering to cede Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai—the six prefectures—to the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 」帝志在盡取江北諸郡，不允其請。

translations.literal: " The emperor's aim was to take all commanderies north of the river and he did not grant the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor aimed to take all territory north of the Yangtze and refused.

sentences.zh: 使人見王師急攻壽陽，李德明奏曰：「願陛下寬臣數日之誅，容臣自往江南，取本國表，盡獻江北之地。

translations.literal: The envoy saw the imperial army urgently attacking Shouyang; Li Deming memorialized: "I beg Your Majesty to spare me execution for a few days and allow me to go myself to Jiangnan to obtain our state's memorial and offer all the land north of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the imperial army pressing Shouyang, Li Deming pleaded: "Grant me a few days' reprieve to return to Jiangnan and bring back a memorial ceding all territory north of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之，乃令李德明、王崇質賫此書以賜李景。

translations.literal: " The emperor granted it and ordered Li Deming and Wang Chongzhi to bear this letter as a gift to Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Li Deming and Wang Chongzhi with this letter to Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子，以徐州節度使武行德為濠州城下行營都部署，以前鄧州節度使候章為壽州城下水寨都部署。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, jiazi: the Xuzhou military governor Wu Xingde was made overall commander of the camp below Haozhou city; the former Dengzhou military governor Hou Zhang was made commander of the water stockade below Shouzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiazi, Wu Xingde of Xuzhou was appointed overall commander below Haozhou, and former Dengzhou governor Hou Zhang was placed in command of the water camp below Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，車駕發壽春，循淮而東。

translations.literal: On jisi, the imperial carriage departed Shouchun and followed the Huai eastward.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor left Shouchun and marched east along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 辛未，揚州奏，江南大破兩浙軍於常州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Yangzhou reported that Jiangnan had greatly defeated the Two Zhes' army at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Yangzhou reported that Jiangnan had routed the Two Zhes' army at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，兩浙錢俶承詔遣部將率兵攻常州，為江南大將陸孟俊所敗，將佐陷沒者甚眾，李景亦以表聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qian Chu of the Two Zhes, by imperial order, had sent a subordinate general to lead troops against Changzhou and was defeated by Jiangnan's great general Lu Mengjun; many officers were lost, and Li Jing also reported it by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qian Chu of the Two Zhes had sent a general against Changzhou by imperial order but was defeated by Jiangnan's Lu Mengjun; many officers were lost. Li Jing reported the victory to the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，駐蹕於濠州城下。

translations.literal: On yihai, the emperor halted below Haozhou city.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor encamped below Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，揚州韓令坤破江南賊軍於州之東境，獲大將陸孟俊。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Han Lingkun of Yangzhou defeated Jiangnan rebel troops on the prefecture's eastern border and captured the great general Lu Mengjun.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Han Lingkun at Yangzhou routed Jiangnan forces on the eastern border and captured Lu Mengjun.

sentences.zh: 今上表大破江南軍於六合，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: The present sovereign memorialized a great defeat of the Jiangnan army at Liuhe, with five thousand heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin reported a major victory over the Jiangnan army at Liuhe, with five thousand heads taken.

sentences.zh: 時李景乘常州之捷，遣陸孟俊領兵迫泰州，王師不守，韓令坤欲棄揚州而回。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing, riding the Changzhou victory, sent Lu Mengjun to lead troops against Taizhou; the imperial army did not hold firm, and Han Lingkun wished to abandon Yangzhou and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by Changzhou, Li Jing sent Lu Mengjun against Taizhou. Zhou forces wavered, and Han Lingkun considered abandoning Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，急遣殿前都指揮使張永德帥親兵往援之，又命今上領步騎二千人屯於六合。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and urgently sent the commander-in-chief of the palace front guard Zhang Yongde to lead personal troops to relieve them; he also ordered the present sovereign to lead two thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor sent Zhang Yongde of the palace guard with elite troops to reinforce Yangzhou and ordered Zhao Kuangyin to camp at Liuhe with two thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 俄而陸孟俊領其徒自海陵抵揚州，令坤迎擊，敗之，生擒孟俊。

translations.literal: Soon Mengjun led his followers from Hailing to Yangzhou; Lingkun met and struck them, defeated them, and captured Mengjun alive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mengjun marched from Hailing on Yangzhou; Lingkun met him, routed his force, and took Mengjun alive.

sentences.zh: 李景遣其弟齊王達率大眾由瓜步濟江，距六合一舍而設柵。

translations.literal: Li Jing sent his younger brother, Prince of Qi Li Da, to lead a great host across the river from Guabu, encamping one li from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sent his brother Li Da, Prince of Qi, with a large army across the river from Guabu to camp a li from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 居數日，乃棄柵來迫官軍。

translations.literal: After several days they abandoned the stockade and came to press the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they abandoned their camp and advanced on the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 今上麾兵以擊之，賊軍大敗，餘眾赴江溺死者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The present sovereign waved his troops to strike; the rebel army was greatly defeated, and the remainder who rushed into the river and drowned could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin led the attack and routed them; countless survivors drowned fleeing into the river.

sentences.zh: 己卯，韓令坤奏，敗楚州賊將馬在貴萬餘眾於灣頭堰，獲漣州刺史秦進崇。

translations.literal: On jimao, Han Lingkun reported defeating more than ten thousand troops under the Chuzhou rebel general Ma Zaigui at Wantou Weir and capturing the Lianzhou prefect Qin Jinchong.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Han Lingkun reported defeating over ten thousand men under the Chuzhou rebel Ma Zaigui at Wantou Weir and capturing Lianzhou prefect Qin Jinchong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以宣徽南院使向訓為權淮南節度使，充沿江招討使；

translations.literal: On bingxu, the commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting Huainan military governor and commissioner for riverine pacification;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Xiang Xun of the southern palace secretariat was made acting Huainan governor and commissioner for riverine pacification;

sentences.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤充沿江副招討使。

translations.literal: the commander-in-chief of the palace horse army Han Lingkun was made deputy commissioner for riverine pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun, commander of the palace horse army, was made his deputy.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《宋史·向拱傳》：揚州初平，南唐令境上出師謀收復，韓令坤有棄城之意，即驛召拱赴行在，拜淮南節度使，依前宣徽使兼沿江招討使，以令坤為副。

translations.literal: (The 《History of Song》, biography of Xiang Gong: When Yangzhou was first pacified, Southern Tang ordered troops on the border to march and plan recovery; Han Lingkun had thoughts of abandoning the city. Gong was summoned by post horse to the imperial camp, appointed Huainan military governor, retaining his former post as secretariat commissioner and also riverine pacification commissioner, with Lingkun as deputy.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of Song》 biography of Xiang Gong records that after Yangzhou fell, Southern Tang tried to recover it and Han Lingkun considered abandoning the city. Gong was summoned to court, made Huainan governor while keeping his secretariat post, and Lingkun was named his deputy.)

sentences.zh: 時周師久駐淮陽，都將趙晁、白延遇等驕恣橫暴，不相稟從，惟務貪濫，至有劫人婦女者。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou army had long encamped at Huaiyang; commanders Zhao Chao, Bai Yanyu, and others were arrogant and violent, would not heed orders, sought only greed and excess, and even seized people's wives and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army had long been encamped at Huaiyang; commanders Zhao Chao and Bai Yanyu grew arrogant and lawless, ignored orders, plundered freely, and even abducted women.

sentences.zh: 及拱至，戮其不法者數輩，軍中肅然。）〉

translations.literal: When Gong arrived, he executed several lawless men, and the army became orderly.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When Gong arrived he executed several offenders, and discipline was restored.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁亥，車駕發濠州，幸渦口。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the imperial carriage departed Haozhou and proceeded to Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor left Haozhou for Wokou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以前湖南節度使馬希崇為左羽林統軍。

translations.literal: On jichou, the former Hunan military governor Ma Xichong was made commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, former Hunan governor Ma Xichong was appointed commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰朔，以渦口為鎮淮軍。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day renchen: Wokou was made the Zhenhuai Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, Wokou was established as the Zhenhuai Army garrison.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還京，發渦口。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the imperial carriage returned to the capital, departing from Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor set out from Wokou on his return to the capital.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：天子駐於渦口，猶欲再幸揚州，宰相範質以師老泣諫，乃班師。）〉

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》: The Son of Heaven halted at Wokou and still wished to visit Yangzhou again; the chief minister Fan Zhi remonstrated with tears that the army was weary, and then the troops were withdrawn.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 records that at Wokou the emperor still meant to march on Yangzhou again until Fan Zhi, weeping, urged that the army was exhausted, whereupon he withdrew.)〉

sentences.zh: 乙卯，上至自淮南，詔赦都下見禁罪人。

translations.literal: On yimao, the emperor arrived from Huainan; an edict pardoned prisoners currently held in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor returned from Huainan and issued an amnesty for prisoners in the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，陳州節度使王令溫卒。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Chenzhou military governor Wang Lingwen died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Chenzhou governor Wang Lingwen died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以江南偽命東都副留守、工部侍郎馮延魯為太府卿。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the falsely appointed Jiangnan eastern-capital deputy regent and Vice Minister of Works Feng Yanlu was made Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the former Jiangnan official Feng Yanlu was appointed director of the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 己未，太子賓客於德辰卒。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the crown prince's mentor Yu Dechen died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, crown prince mentor Yu Dechen died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔：「天下公私織造布帛及諸色匹段，幅尺斤兩，並須依向來制度，不得輕弱假偽，犯者擒捉送官。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict: "Throughout the realm, whether public or private weaving of cloth and silks and all sorts of bolt goods—width, measure, weight—must all follow the former regulations; light, weak, or counterfeit goods are forbidden; offenders are to be seized and sent to the authorities."
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou an edict ordered that all cloth and silk woven for public or private use must meet established standards of width, length, and weight, forbidding shoddy or counterfeit goods on pain of arrest.

sentences.zh: 六月甲子，以鳳翔節度使王景為秦州節度使，兼西面沿邊都部署；

translations.literal: Sixth month, jiazi: the Fengxiang military governor Wang Jing was made Qinzhou military governor and also overall commander along the western frontier;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Jing of Fengxiang was made Qinzhou governor and overall frontier commander in the west;

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使、陳州節度使向訓為淮南節度使，依前南院宣徽使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: the commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Chenzhou military governor Xiang Xun was made Huainan military governor, retaining his former southern-bureau secretariat post, with the added title of Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun was confirmed as Huainan governor while keeping his secretariat post, with the honorary title of Grand Guardian;

sentences.zh: 以曹州節度使韓通為許州節度使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: the Caozhou military governor Han Tong was made Xuzhou military governor, with the added title of Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong was transferred from Caozhou to Xuzhou with the honorary title of Grand Guardian;

sentences.zh: 以亳州防禦使王全斌為隴州防禦使，遙領利州昭武軍兩使留後。

translations.literal: the Bozhou defense commissioner Wang Quanbin was made Longzhou defense commissioner, and at a distance held the two military commissionerships of Lizhou and the Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin was moved from Bozhou to Longzhou and given distant oversight of Lizhou and the Zhaowu Army.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，許州王彥超移鎮永興軍，鄧州田景鹹移鎮鄜州。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Wang Yanchao of Xuzhou was transferred to Yongxing Army; Tian Jingxian of Dengzhou was transferred to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Wang Yanchao was transferred from Xuzhou to Yongxing, and Tian Jingxian from Dengzhou to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞楊昭儉、知雜侍御史趙礪、侍御史張糾並停任，坐鞫獄失實也。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Yang Zhaojian, the supervising miscellaneous-affairs attendant censor Zhao Li, and the attendant censor Zhang Jiu were all suspended from office for errors in trying cases.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Yang Zhaojian, supervising censor Zhao Li, and attendant censor Zhang Jiu were all removed from office for mishandling criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎陶穀為兵部侍郎，充翰林學士承旨；

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Tao Gu was made Vice Minister of War and served as chief Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Tao Gu was made vice minister of war and chief Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以水部員外郎知制誥扈載、度支員外郎王著，並本官充翰林學士；

translations.literal: the Water Bureau vice director and drafter of edicts Hu Zai and the Revenue Bureau vice director Wang Zhu, each in their original rank, were made Hanlin academicians;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zai and Wang Zhu were appointed Hanlin academicians while keeping their existing ranks;

sentences.zh: 以給事中高防為右散騎常侍；

translations.literal: the Supervising Secretary Gao Fang was made Right Regular Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fang was promoted to Right Regular Attendant;

sentences.zh: 以前都官郎中、知制誥薛居正為左諫議大夫，充昭文館學士，判館事。

translations.literal: the former Capital Crimes Bureau director and drafter of edicts Xue Juzheng was made Left Remonstrance Grand Master, academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and administrator of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Juzheng was made Left Remonstrance Grand Master, Zhaowen Hall academician, and administrator of the hall.

sentences.zh: 壬申，曲赦淮南道諸州見禁罪人，自今年六月十一日已前，凡有違犯，無問輕重，並不窮問。

translations.literal: On renshen, a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners held in the prefectures of the Huainan circuit: for all offenses before the eleventh day of the sixth month of this year, regardless of severity, no further inquiry would be made.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen a partial amnesty covered all prisoners in Huainan for offenses committed before the eleventh of the sixth month, without regard to severity.

sentences.zh: 先屬江南之時，應有非理科徭，無名配率，一切停罷雲。

translations.literal: For the period when they had belonged to Jiangnan, all improper corvée and nameless extra levies were entirely halted.
translations.idiomatic: All improper corvée and unauthorized levies dating from Jiangnan rule were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以右衛上將軍扈彥珂為太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Right Guard senior general Hu Yanke was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Hu Yanke of the Right Guard was retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以西京留守王晏為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the western-capital regent Wang Yan was made Fengxiang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, western-capital regent Wang Yan was appointed Fengxiang governor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，升贍國軍為濱州。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the Shanguo Army was promoted to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Shanguo Army district was elevated to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮南道招討使李重進奏，壽州賊軍攻南寨，王師不利。

translations.literal: The Huainan circuit pacification commissioner Li Chongjin reported that Shouzhou rebel troops attacked the southern stockade and the imperial army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin reported that Shouzhou rebels had attacked the southern camp and the imperial forces had suffered a setback.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔步軍都指揮使李繼勛營於壽州之南，攻賊壘。

translations.literal: Earlier, the foot-army commander-in-chief Li Jixun had been ordered to encamp south of Shouzhou and attack rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jixun, commander of the foot army, had been ordered to camp south of Shouzhou and assault the rebel works.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊軍出城來攻我軍，破柵而入，其攻城之具並為賊所焚，將士死者數百人。

translations.literal: That day the rebel army came out of the city to attack our army, broke through the stockade and entered; their siege equipment was all burned by the rebels, and several hundred officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rebels sallied out, broke into the camp, burned the siege equipment, and killed several hundred Zhou soldiers.

sentences.zh: 李重進在東寨，亦不能救。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin was in the eastern stockade and could not rescue them either.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin in the eastern camp was unable to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 時城堅未下，師老於外，加之暑毒，糧運不繼。

translations.literal: At the time the city was strong and had not fallen; the army was weary from long campaigning abroad, and moreover summer heat was fierce and grain transport did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou still held out; the army was worn down by the long siege, summer heat was brutal, and supplies ran short.

sentences.zh: 李繼勛喪失之後，軍無固誌，諸將議欲退軍，賴今上自六合領兵歸闕，過其城下，因為駐留旬日，王師復振。

translations.literal: After Li Jixun's defeat the army had no firm will; the generals discussed withdrawing. Thanks to the present sovereign leading troops back to the capital from Liuhe and passing below the city, he halted there for ten days and the imperial army revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Jixun's defeat morale collapsed and the generals talked of withdrawal. Zhao Kuangyin, returning from Liuhe to court, paused below the city for ten days and restored the army's spirit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛卯朔，以武清軍節度使、知潭州軍府事周行逢為朗州大都督，充武平軍節度使，加檢校太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day xinmao: the Wuqing Army military governor and acting Tanzhou prefect Zhou Xingfeng was made great governor of Lang Prefecture and Wuping Army military governor, with the added titles of Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month of autumn, Zhou Xingfeng was made great governor of Langzhou and Wuping Army governor, with the honorary titles of Grand Guardian and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以太子賓客盧價為禮部尚書致仕，以給事中李明為大理卿。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the crown prince's mentor Lu Jia was made Minister of Rites and retired; the Supervising Secretary Li Ming was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, crown prince mentor Lu Jia retired as Minister of Rites, and Supervising Secretary Li Ming was appointed director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 庚子，盧州行營都部署劉重進奏，破淮賊千餘於州界。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Luzhou campaign commander Liu Chongjin reported defeating more than a thousand Huainan rebels on the prefecture border.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Liu Chongjin at Luzhou reported defeating over a thousand Huainan rebels on the border.

sentences.zh: 丁未，濠州行營都部署武行德奏，敗淮賊二千人於州界。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Haozhou campaign commander Wu Xingde reported defeating two thousand Huainan rebels on the prefecture border.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Wu Xingde at Haozhou reported defeating two thousand Huainan rebels on the border.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，太子太保王仁裕卒。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Wang Renyu died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Wang Renyu died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，皇后符氏薨。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Empress Fu died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Empress Fu died.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使向訓自揚州班師，回駐壽春。

translations.literal: The Huainan military governor Xiang Xun withdrew his army from Yangzhou and returned to encamp at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun withdrew from Yangzhou and re-established headquarters at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 時王師攻壽春，經年未下，江、淮盜賊充斥，舒、蘄、和、泰等州復為吳人所據，故棄揚州並力於壽春焉。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army had attacked Shouchun for a year without taking it; bandits filled the Yangtze and Huai regions, and Shu, Qi, He, Tai, and other prefectures had again been seized by Wu men—therefore Yangzhou was abandoned to concentrate force on Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Shouchun had dragged on for a year; banditry spread along the rivers, and Shu, Qi, He, Tai, and other prefectures had fallen back to the Wu. Xiang Xun therefore abandoned Yangzhou to concentrate on Shouchun.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：向訓請棄揚州，並力以攻壽春，乃封府庫付主者，遣淮南舊將按巡城中，秋毫不犯而去。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》: Xun requested abandoning Yangzhou to concentrate force on attacking Shouchun; he sealed the treasury and entrusted it to custodians, sent former Huainan generals to patrol the city, and departed without violating so much as an autumn hair.)
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling records that Xun asked to abandon Yangzhou for Shouchun, sealed the treasury, posted former Huainan officers to keep order, and withdrew without harming the populace.)

sentences.zh: 淮人大悅，皆負糗糧以送周師。）〉

translations.literal: The Huai people were greatly pleased and all carried dry rations to send off the Zhou army.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The local people were delighted and brought provisions to see the Zhou troops off.)〉

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，河陽白重贊移鎮涇州，張澤移鎮河中。

translations.literal: Eighth month, renxu: Bai Chongzan of Heyang was transferred to Jing Prefecture; Zhang Ze was transferred to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renxu, Bai Chongzan was transferred from Heyang to Jingzhou and Zhang Ze to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以前鄧州節度使侯章復為鄧州節度使，以侍衛步軍都指揮使、彰信軍節度使李繼勛為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the former Dengzhou military governor Hou Zhang was again made Dengzhou military governor; the foot-army commander-in-chief and Zhangxin Army military governor Li Jixun was made Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Hou Zhang was restored to Dengzhou, and Li Jixun was transferred from the Zhangxin Army to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，太僕卿劇可久停任，坐為舉官累也。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Director of the Imperial Stud Ju Kejiu was suspended from office for being implicated through a nominee he had recommended.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Director of the Imperial Stud Ju Kejiu was removed from office because a man he had recommended was implicated in wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，端明殿學士王樸撰成新歷上之，命曰《顯德欽天曆》，上親為制序，仍付司天監行用。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Academician of the Duanming Hall Wang Pu completed a new calendar and presented it; it was named the 《Xiande Reverence-of-Heaven Calendar》; the emperor personally composed the preface and ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to put it into use.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wang Pu presented the new 《Xiande Reverence-of-Heaven Calendar》 with a preface by the emperor himself; the Directorate of Astronomy was ordered to adopt it.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使張永德奏，破淮賊於下蔡。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief of the palace front guard Zhang Yongde reported defeating Huainan rebels at Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde, commander of the palace front guard, reported defeating Huainan rebels at Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 先是，江南李景以王師猶在壽州，遣其將林仁肇、郭廷謂率水陸軍至下蔡，欲奪浮梁，以舟實薪芻，乘風縱火，永德禦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Jing of Jiangnan, because the imperial army was still at Shouzhou, sent his generals Lin Renzhao and Guo Tingyu to lead land and water forces to Xiaocai, intending to seize the floating bridge; they loaded boats with firewood and fodder and, riding the wind, set fires—Yongde defended against them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jing had sent Lin Renzhao and Guo Tingyu with a combined force to Xiaocai to seize the pontoon bridge, loading fire ships with fuel and straw. Yongde met the attack.

sentences.zh: 有頃，風勢倒指，賊眾稍卻，因為官軍所敗。

translations.literal: After a while the wind shifted direction, the rebel host fell back somewhat, and they were therefore defeated by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the wind shifted against them, the enemy fell back, and the imperial troops routed them.

sentences.zh: 己卯，工部侍郎王敏停任，坐薦子婿陳南金為河陽記室也。

translations.literal: On jimao, Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was suspended from office for having recommended his son-in-law Chen Nanjin as Heyang secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was removed from office for appointing his son-in-law Chen Nanjin as secretariat aide at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午，以端明殿學士、左散騎常侍、權知開封府事王樸為尚書戶部侍郎，充樞密副使；

translations.literal: Ninth month, bingwu: the Duanming Hall academician, Left Regular Attendant, and acting Kaifeng prefect Wang Pu was made Vice Minister of Revenue in the Ministry of Revenue and served as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, Wang Pu was made vice minister of revenue and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以右羽林統軍焦繼勛為左屯衛上將軍；

translations.literal: the commander of the Right Feathered Forest Army Jiao Jixun was made senior general of the Left Encampment Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Jixun was transferred from the Right to the Left Feathered Forest Army as senior general;

sentences.zh: 以左衛上將軍楊承信為右羽林統軍；

translations.literal: the Left Guard senior general Yang Chengxin was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest Army;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest Army;

sentences.zh: 以左監門上將軍宋延渥為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: the Left Gate senior general Song Yanwo was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yanwo was appointed commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛酉，葬宣懿皇后於懿陵。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, xinyou: Empress Xuanyi was buried at Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on xinyou, Empress Xuanyi was interred at Yiling.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以右神武統軍宋延渥為廬州行營副部署。

translations.literal: On guihai, the commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Song Yanwo was made deputy commander of the Luzhou campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Song Yanwo, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was appointed deputy commander of the Luzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，舒州刺史郭令圖責授虢州教練使，坐棄郡逃歸也。

translations.literal: On yichou, Shuzhou prefect Guo Lingtu was demoted and appointed training commissioner of Guo Prefecture for having abandoned his commandery and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Guo Lingtu of Shuzhou was demoted to training commissioner at Guozhou for abandoning his post and fleeing home.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「諸司職員皆系奏補，當執役之際，悉藉公勤，及聽選之時，尤資幹敏，茍非慎擇，漸致因循。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict said: "Staff of all offices are appointed by memorial; when they perform duties, all rely on public diligence, and at the time of selection especially need capability and alertness. If selection is not careful, sloth will gradually arise."
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an edict declared that all office staff were appointed by memorial and must be chosen for diligence and ability, warning that careless selection would breed complacency.

sentences.zh: 應諸司寺監，今後收補役人，並須人材俊利，身言可采，書劄堪中，自前行止，委無訛濫，勒本司關送吏部，引驗人材，考校筆劄。

translations.literal: All directorates and commissions of offices henceforth, when recruiting service personnel, must require talented and sharp men whose person and speech are acceptable, whose documents pass standard, whose past conduct is truly without fraud—compel the home office to forward them to the Ministry of Personnel, present them for verification of talent, and examine their writing.
translations.idiomatic: All offices must hereafter recruit only capable men of good character and competent writing, certify their records, and send them to the Ministry of Personnel for examination.

sentences.zh: 其中選者，連所試書跡及正身引過中書，余從前後格敕處分，仍每年只得一度奏補。

translations.literal: Those chosen among them, together with their trial calligraphy and in person, were led past the Secretariat; the rest were handled according to former regulations and edicts, and each year only one round of memorial appointment was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Successful candidates were presented in person with their writing samples to the Secretariat; other matters followed existing regulations, and appointments by memorial were limited to once per year.

sentences.zh: 」丁卯，宣懿皇后神主入廟，時有司請為後立別廟，禮也。

translations.literal: " On dingmao, the spirit tablet of Empress Xuanyi entered the temple; at that time the relevant offices requested a separate temple for the empress—this was ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the spirit tablet of Empress Xuanyi was installed in the ancestral temple; the ritual offices properly requested a separate shrine for the empress.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔：「漳河以北郡縣，並許鹽貨通商，逐處有鹼鹵之地，一任人戶煎煉。

translations.literal: On jisi, an edict: "In commanderies and counties north of the Zhang River, salt goods may all be traded; wherever there are alkaline brine lands, households are permitted to boil and refine salt."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict permitted salt trade in all counties north of the Zhang River and allowed households to boil salt wherever brine deposits existed.

sentences.zh: 」壬申，以武平軍節度副使、知潭州軍府事宇文瓊為武清軍節度使，知潭州軍府事。

translations.literal: " On renshen, the Wuping Army deputy military governor and acting Tanzhou prefect Yuwen Qiong was made Wuqing Army military governor and acting Tanzhou prefect.
