translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Yuwen Qiong was made Wuqing Army governor while continuing as acting Tanzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，淮南招討使李重進奏，破淮賊於盛唐，斬二千級。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Huainan pacification commissioner Li Chongjin reported defeating Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang, with two thousand heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Li Chongjin reported defeating Huainan rebels at Sheng Tang and taking two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 太子賓客致仕薛仁謙卒。

translations.literal: The retired crown prince's mentor Xue Renqian died.
translations.idiomatic: Retired crown prince mentor Xue Renqian died.

sentences.zh: 丙子，襄州節度使、守太尉、兼中書令、陳王安審琦加守太師。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Xiangzhou military governor, Grand Guardian, concurrent Secretariat Director, and Prince of Chen Wang Shenqi was further made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Prince of Chen Wang Shenqi of Xiangzhou was promoted to Grand Preceptor while retaining his other honors.

sentences.zh: 審琦鎮漢上十餘年，至是來朝，故以命寵之。

translations.literal: Shenqi had governed the Han region for more than ten years; now he came to court, and therefore this appointment honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi had governed the Han River region for over ten years and had now come to court, and this appointment was meant to honor him.

sentences.zh: 癸未，右拾遺趙守微杖一百，配沙門島。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Right Reminder Zhao Shouwei was beaten one hundred strokes and exiled to Shamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Right Reminder Zhao Shouwei was flogged a hundred strokes and exiled to Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 守微本村民也，形貌樸野，粗學為文。

translations.literal: Shouwei had originally been a village man, plain and rustic in appearance, with rough learning in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwei was a villager by origin, plain in appearance, with only rudimentary literary training.

sentences.zh: 前年徒步上書，帝以急於取士，授右拾遺，聞者駭其事。

translations.literal: The year before last he went on foot to submit a memorial; the emperor, eager to obtain talent, appointed him Right Reminder, and those who heard were astonished at the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Two years earlier he had walked to court with a memorial; eager for talent, the emperor made him Right Reminder, to widespread astonishment.

sentences.zh: 至是為妻父所訟，彰其醜行，故逐之。

translations.literal: Now he was sued by his wife's father, who exposed his shameful conduct, and therefore he was expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Now his father-in-law sued him and exposed his misconduct, leading to his expulsion.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·張昭傳》云：世宗好拔奇取俊，有自布衣上書、下僚言事者，多不次進用。

translations.literal: (The 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》, biography of Zhang Zhao, says: Shizong loved to raise the extraordinary and select the outstanding; those who submitted memorials as commoners or spoke on affairs as junior officials were often promoted out of turn.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Zhang Zhao biography in the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 records that Shizong favored promoting unusual talent and often advanced commoners who submitted memorials or junior officials who spoke up.)

sentences.zh: 昭諫曰：「昔唐初劉洎、馬周起徒步，太宗擢用為相，其後朱樸、柳璨在下僚，昭宗亦以大用，然則太宗用之於前而國興，昭宗用於後而國亡，士之難知也如此。

translations.literal: Zhao remonstrated: "In early Tang, Liu Ji and Ma Zhou rose from foot soldiers; Taizong promoted them to chancellor. Later Zhu Pu and Liu Can were junior officials whom Zhaozong also greatly employed—yet Taizong used men in the former case and the state flourished; Zhaozong used them in the latter case and the state perished. How hard it is to know men!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao remonstrated: "In early Tang, Liu Ji and Ma Zhou rose from humble origins and Taizong made them chancellors. Later Zhu Pu and Liu Can were promoted by Zhaozong from junior posts—yet Taizong's choices strengthened the state while Zhaozong's destroyed it. Talent is hard to judge."

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下存舊法而用人，以劉、馬為鑒，朱、柳為戒，則善矣。」）〉

translations.literal: " Your subject wishes Your Majesty to keep the old methods in employing men, take Liu and Ma as mirrors and Zhu and Liu as warnings—then it would be well.")〉
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to follow established methods of appointment, taking Liu and Ma as models and Zhu and Liu as warnings.")〉

sentences.zh: 甲申，宣授今上同州節度使兼殿前都指揮使，宣授內外馬步軍都軍頭袁彥為曹州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the present sovereign was announced and appointed Tongzhou military governor and concurrent commander-in-chief of the palace front guard; Yuan Yan, chief of all internal and external horse and foot armies, was announced and appointed Caozhou military governor and concurrent commander-in-chief of the palace foot guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Zhao Kuangyin was formally appointed Tongzhou governor and commander of the palace front guard; Yuan Yan, chief of all horse and foot armies, was made Caozhou governor and commander of the palace foot guard.

sentences.zh: 戊子，右神武統軍張彥超卒。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Zhang Yanchao died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Zhang Yanchao, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, died.

sentences.zh: 十一月己丑朔，詔廢天下無名祠廟。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day jichou: an edict abolished unauthorized shrines throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, an edict abolished unauthorized shrines throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 庚子，日南至，帝不受朝賀，以宣懿皇后遷祔日近也。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the winter solstice; the emperor did not receive court congratulations, because the day for transferring Empress Xuanyi's tablet to joint enshrinement was near.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the winter solstice, the emperor declined court homage because the rites for installing Empress Xuanyi's tablet were imminent.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，江南進奉使孫晟下獄死，江南進奉使鐘謨責授耀州司馬。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Jiangnan tribute envoy Sun Sheng died in prison; the Jiangnan tribute envoy Zhong Mo was demoted and appointed Yazhou marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Jiangnan envoy Sun Sheng died in prison; Zhong Mo was demoted to marshal at Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，放華山隱者陳摶歸山。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Huashan recluse Chen Tuan was released to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the Huashan recluse Chen Tuan was released to return to his mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝素聞摶有道術，征之赴闕，月餘放還舊隱。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard that Tuan possessed the Way and arts; he was summoned to court and after more than a month was released to his former seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long heard of Tuan's mastery of the Way, summoned him to court, and after a month sent him back to his retreat.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，殿前都指揮使張永德奏，敗濠州送糧軍二千人於下蔡，奪米船十餘艘。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the commander-in-chief of the palace front guard Zhang Yongde reported defeating two thousand Haozhou grain-escort troops at Xiaocai and seizing more than ten rice boats.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Zhang Yongde reported defeating two thousand Haozhou grain convoy troops at Xiaocai and capturing more than ten supply boats.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李穀以風痹請告十旬，三上表求解所任，不允。

translations.literal: The chief minister Li Gu, owing to wind paralysis, requested leave for ten ten-day periods and three times memorialized to be released from his post; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Li Gu, suffering from paralysis, requested three months' leave and three times asked to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未朔，以給事中張鑄為光祿卿，鑄訴以官名與祖諱同，尋改秘書監，判光祿寺事。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, first day jiwei: the Supervising Secretary Zhang Zhu was made Director of the Imperial Banquets; Zhu pleaded that the office name matched his ancestor's taboo name, and soon was changed to Director of the Secretariat, administering the Imperial Banquets Office.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, Zhang Zhu was appointed director of imperial banquets but pleaded that the title matched his ancestor's taboo name; he was soon made director of the Secretariat while overseeing the banquets office.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以許州節度使韓通兼侍衛馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Xuzhou military governor Han Tong was also made chief adjutant of the palace horse and foot guards.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Han Tong of Xuzhou was also appointed chief adjutant of the palace horse and foot guards.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以右領軍大將軍、權判三司張美領三司使。

translations.literal: On renxu, the Right Army senior general and acting administrator of the Three Departments Zhang Mei was made commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Zhang Mei was appointed commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以滑州節度使兼殿前都指揮使、駙馬都尉張永德為殿前都點校。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Huazhou military governor, concurrent commander-in-chief of the palace front guard, and imperial son-in-law Zhang Yongde was made chief inspector of the palace front guard.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Zhang Yongde was appointed chief inspector of the palace front guard while retaining his governorship and command.

sentences.zh: 發陳、蔡、宋、亳、潁、曹、單等州丁夫城下蔡。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers were levied from Chen, Cai, Song, Bo, Ying, Cao, Shan, and other prefectures to fortify Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée laborers from Chen, Cai, Song, Bo, Ying, Cao, Shan, and other prefectures were mobilized to fortify Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，故襄邑令劉居方贈右補闕，男士衡賜學究出身，獎廉吏也。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the former magistrate of Xiangyi Liu Jufang was posthumously made Right Supplementation Censor; his son Shiheng was granted the status of classical scholar graduate—to reward an incorrupt official.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the late magistrate of Xiangyi Liu Jufang was posthumously honored as Right Supplementation Censor and his son Shiheng granted scholar status, in reward for upright service.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔兵部尚書張昭纂修太祖實錄及梁均王、唐清泰帝兩朝實錄。

translations.literal: On guihai, an edict ordered Minister of War Zhang Zhao to compile the Veritable Records of the Grand Ancestor and the veritable records of the two reigns of Liang's Prince Jun and Tang's Emperor Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai an edict ordered Zhang Zhao to compile the Veritable Records of Taizu and the records of the Liang and Tang reigns of Prince Jun and Emperor Qingtai.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》云：同修撰官委張昭定名奏請，至四年正月，張昭奏請國子祭酒尹拙、太子詹事劉溫叟同編修。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 says: Co-compilers were entrusted to Zhang Zhao to determine names and memorialize; by the first month of the fourth year, Zhang Zhao memorialized requesting the Director of the Imperial Academy Yin Zhuo and the Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Liu Wensou to compile jointly.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that Zhang Zhao was to name co-compilers; in the first month of year four he proposed Yin Zhuo and Liu Wensou as joint compilers.)〉

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「史館所少書籍，宜令本館諸處求訪補填。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Books lacking in the History Office should be sought and supplied from all places by the office."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered the History Office to search widely for books missing from its collection.

sentences.zh: 如有收得書籍之家，並許進書人據部帙多少等第，各與恩澤，如是卷帙少者，量給資帛。

translations.literal: If there are households that have collected books, all are permitted to present books; according to the number of fascicles, grades of favor are given; if the rolls are few, compensation in goods and silks is allotted as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Households possessing books were invited to present them, with rewards graded by the number of volumes; smaller donations received proportionate payment in goods and silk.

sentences.zh: 如館內已有之書，不在進納之限。

translations.literal: Books already in the office are not within the limit for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Books already held by the office were not eligible for presentation rewards.

sentences.zh: 仍委中書門下，於朝官內選差三十人，據見在書籍，各求真本校勘，署校官姓名，逐月具功課申報中書門下。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was further entrusted to select thirty men from court officials; according to existing books, each was to collate authentic texts, sign the collator's name, and each month report accomplishments to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was to select thirty court officials to collate the existing collection, sign their work, and report monthly on their progress.
